# Probable Cause Any combination of the following constitutes probable cause for arrest:
## Eyewitness reports from any security or command member. - This includes a security member watching someone commit a crime. Witnessing a crime constitutes probable cause.
## Self admission of a crime by a suspect.
## Reports from the Station AI of a crime. - This does not include borgs, who, for the purposes of probable cause, are treated as a regular crew report.
## Overwhelming evidence - This means that if a security officer arrives at the scene of a crime and finds a suspect surrounded in a pool of blood, with a weapon and a body, there is probable cause for an arrest, regardless of whether or not any security or command witnessed the actual murder. - This also includes fingerprints found on weapons or other contraband, and door logs. - This does not mean that multiple reports from non security or command members constitute “overwhelming evidence”; please see the section on “reports from non security or command members” below.
## Not enough to constitute probable cause The following are not enough to constitute probable cause:
### Reports from non security or command members - In the case of credible reports from non security or command members, regular arrest protocol should be followed, where a search warrant or arrest warrant is drawn up by normal procedures. - This does *not* mean that security cannot go to the scene of a reported crime. Security should respond to reports of threats; often, overwhelming evidence can be found through such reports (such as arriving to a very conspicuous murder scene with a suspect). This simply means that the reports alone are not enough to create probable cause.
### Proximity to a crime scene without other evidence. - Sometimes people are just poking through maintenance looking for plushies.
# Method of Escalation (Ordinary Arrests) If security has probable cause, arrests should be made utilizing the following method of escalation:
## 1) Verbal Command
### a) Make it clear that the individual is under arrest, and that they must not resist. - i) Example: “You are under arrest. Please do not resist.”
### b) If the suspect complies, skip to step 4.
### c) If the suspect does not comply, continue to step 2.
### d) If the suspect has started to run, skip to step 3.
### e) - If the suspect has responded violently - skip to step 3 or step 5 if necessary - Officers should prioritize less-lethal containment if reasonable.
## 2) Declare Intention to Escalate to less-than-lethal methods
### a) Declare that you will use less-than-lethal force if the suspect continues resisting. - i) Example: “I will stun you if you do not comply.”
### b) If the suspect complies, skip to step 4.
### c) If the suspect does not comply, continue to step 3.
### d) If the suspect has been running for some time and commands cannot be issued, use good judgement before moving to step 3 without declaring an intention to escalate to less-than-lethals.
## 3) Use Less-Lethal Methods of Containment
### a) This includes disablers, dual-setting energy weapons set to stun, stun batons, and bolas. - i) Flashes can be used at this step if deemed useful. Do not use flashes without cause, as they are very painful to Shadekin crewmembers. - ii) EMPs may be used at this step on crew members or borgs that would be affected by such weapons. Avoid using EMPs if they risk downing your own security team members. - iii) Rubber bullets can be used for particularly belligerent individuals; they should be avoided if possible.
### b) Do not continue stunning the suspect once they have been downed.
### c) Do not use a stun baton that is not set to stun during this step.
### d) If the suspect resists violently, continue to step 5.
### e) Once the suspect is downed, continue to step 4.
## 3) Detain the Suspect
### a) Cuff the suspect with handcuffs if available. - i) Zipties should only be used as a last case resort.
### b) Tell the suspect that any questions about their arrest will be answered in security, and not enroute, if necessary.
### c) Take the suspect to security promptly.
### d) Do not harm the suspect once cuffed.
### e) Once the suspect is secured inside of Security, use the Criminal Records Computer to update their status to “DETAINED”. You may also notify another member of the department to do this.
## 5) OPTIONAL, WORST CASE SCENARIO Use Lethal Methods of Containment
### a) This includes firearms, including longarms, laser weapons, and all forms of melee weapons if deemed reasonable. - i) This does not include any heavy weapons.
### b) Once the suspect is downed, detain them as one would in step 4, per the following: - i) Do not continue to harm the suspect once they are downed. - ii) Cuff the suspect, *then* administer basic first aid if necessary. - The emergency medipen is a valuable tool and is often enough to keep suspects alive long enough for the corpsman or other medical staff to do their job back in security. - iii) Take the suspect to security as usual, but first radio that they will need medical attention on security comms, and ensure that medical attention is ready to be administered promptly. - iv) If you have been injured and may not make it back to security without passing out, call for backup immediately.
### c) Minimize lethal methods of containment in crowded areas of the station where possible.
# Method of Escalation (Station Threats) The Method of Escalation (Station Threats) should *only* ever be applied to emergency, station-level threats that have been proven hostile, as listed below. such as Space Dragons or coordinated attacks against the station. When in doubt, use the Method of Escalation (Ordinary Arrests).
Station Threats include the following entities and dangers when they are proven hostile: - Space Dragons - Colossus - Revenants - Nuclear Operatives - Robo-Neuroticists - Ninjas - Rat Kings - Trash Lizards
When dealing with one of these Station Threats that have proven themselves to be hostile to the station and its crew:
## 1) Communicate the threat.
### a) When possible, announce the threat over security comms. - The Head of Security should make a communications console announcement of the threat when possible, or get another command member to do so.
### b) In absolute emergencies, announce the threat over general comms.
## 2) Attempt to contain the threat.
### a) Station Threats pose significant danger to the crew. Attempt to keep them away from populated areas of the station.
### b) Some threats will be more difficult to contain. If a threat can be eliminated quickly, prioritize efficiency over absolute containment.
## 3) Necessary force Use necessary force to efficiently negate the threat.
### a) Station destruction should be avoided where possible This is not always possible. Deal with the threat efficiently.
### b) Bystander safety Prioritize bystander safety, but not to the detriment of negating the threat.
## 4) Call reinforcements early and communicate often.
## 5) In the case of downed threats Revival is not necessary, nor is medical care. Ensure the threat is neutralized and secured before considering medical care.
### a) This can include humanely ending suffering if necessary. This should be done with an efficient incision to the neck or lethal ammunition to the head. - i) This should not be done with blunt melee, lethal substances, or flame. - ii) This should not be done with unnecessary violence, force, or derogatory remarks. Finish the threat quickly, humanely, and without insult. - iii) This should be done in the field. Do not administer medical care first. - iv) If a threat receives medical care in security, they must be removed by GALPOL for execution, and not executed after receiving care. - v) If the officer is uncomfortable doing this, the threat can be taken back to security for extradition by GALPOL instead.
### b) Restraining the threat - Restraining the threat with handcuffs is a valid form of neutralization. - Any contraband, restricted, or otherwise potentially dangerous items must be secured quickly, and before revival or medical care. - If the threat has received medical care after being neutralized, they must be contained within the Permanent Confinement Area. - Neutralized threats that have received medical care and are in the Permanent Confinement Area are given the same rights as all other prisoners.
# Handling the “Devil” On rare occasions, an otherworldly entity referred to as “a devil” or “the devil” will manifest and infiltrate the station with the intent to make illicit dealings. These entities have committed Identity Fraud, as they are illegally taking the appearance of another person. Any “deal” made with a devil is also innately illegal for all parties involved, under the crime of Black Marketeering. Some aspects of a deal may also be their own crimes, such as taking someone’s soul being Prevention of Revival. **A devil can only be confirmed if they admit to being a devil, or if they have made a deal with another crew member.**
When a devil has been identified, Security personnel must not engage with the devil without the support of the Chaplain or Mystagogue, unless absolutely necessary to immediately protect the station and its crew. Devils cannot be truly killed or contained with Security measures alone, and Security must coordinate with the Chaplain and Mystagogue to “banish” the devil when they are critically injured. These banishments are often temporary, so continued coordination through the shift is recommended.
When they have been discovered and hunted, some devils may choose to submit and surrender to station security. If this happens, the devil is given the same rights as any other prisoner, and must be held in the permanent confinement area. If the Devil attempts to escape permanent confinement, Security must once again banish them with the assistance of the Chaplain and Mystagogue.
